quote: The multi-contour seats in my X5 were the best car seats, the GV80 seats are passable at best.
I went to drive a base Macan right afterwards and we agreed gv70 drove better. Macan little less body roll but not by much. Gv70 more comfortable ride but still felt very planted.

I can honestly say that compared to all the other cars I researched deeply and test drove, the GV80 is clearly, for me, the best. The only car that came close was the BMW x5, and I feel the GV80 is better than that.

I have found, in this short experience, the GV80 to be just astonishingly nice to drive - composed, comfortable, quiet, smooth ride. The only car that came close was the BMW x5, and I feel the GV80 is better than that.
BMWs X5 ... had very comfortable and supportive seating evidenced and appreciated on long drives. Unfortunately the 2021 GV80 Advanced had none of the seating comfort.
The interior of the XC90 has much refined and nicer finish with a better ergonomics for us. The R1S driver's seat lacks lateral support both the seat cushion and the back.
On a long road trips (~400 miles/day), I recall XC90 being less tiring than the R1S.

We traded our 2017 hybrid Volvo because we were much more experienced with EV's and got our R1s last year. The Volvos front seats and stereo were superior and I feel the fit and finish was also better.
I jumped in the Tahoe to get the kids this afternoon and said, I don't ever need to drive the Rivian again. This is more comfortable, has HUD, rides better and is as quiet.
